title: Identical Primitive Identifier Swap
pattern: Function signatures taking multiple parameters of the exact same primitive type representing different domain identifiers.
why_bad: Because both arguments are of the same primitive type (e.g., `u64`), the compiler cannot detect when a developer accidentally swaps the order of arguments at the call site. This leads to silent logic bypasses and data mismatches.
detection: Adjacent or near-adjacent function parameters ending in `_id` that share an identical primitive type.
counterexample:
A generic comparison function explicitly designed to operate on two identical ID spaces:
```rust
fn are_matching(id1: u64, id2: u64) -> bool { id1 == id2 }
```
